finding.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` changes semantics for *all* bounded ranges, breaking position-dependent and paired-range functions
finding.evidence: The new block `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; }` is applied to every range argument, not just expanded unbounded ones. Any function whose semantics depend on the *number* or *ordinal position* of cells in a range (MATCH/INDEX-style lookups, COUNTBLANK, ROWS/COLUMNS-ish helpers, or paired ranges such as SUMIF(range, crit, sum_range) / SUMPRODUCT) now receives a compacted, misaligned stream: e.g. `=MATCH(x, A1:A10, 0)` returns the index within the non-blank subset, not within the range. It also changes pre-existing results for bounded ranges (`=AVERAGE(A1:A3)` with A2 blank goes from 13.33 to 20) — an intentional Excel alignment, but one applied far outside the stated scope, and an all-blank range now yields zero arguments where callers previously always got N arguments (functions that reduce without an initial value can throw or return an error instead of 0).
